text: writing and running a Python script for novice users: 1. Install Python (if not using Colab): The team guides users on how to install Python using Anaconda or directly from the official website. 2. Set Up Your Environment (if not using colab): The team explains how to open a terminal or command prompt, create a new directory for a project, and navigate to this directory. 3. Create a New Script (if not using Colab): The team shows how to open a text editor or an IDE (like VSCode or PyCharm) and create a new file named hello_ai.py. 4. Write the First Code (all users): The team provides a simple code example that directs Python to generate fake sensor data over time, which can be executed by a beginner without importing data: python import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np # Generate fake time series data np.random.seed(42) # For reproducibility time = np.arange(0, 100, 1) # 100 time points sensor_data = np.sin(time / 10) + np.random.normal(0, 0.1, size=time.shape) # Sine wave with noise # Create a scatter plot plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6)) plt.scatter(time, sensor_data, color='b', label='Sensor Data', alpha=0.6) # Add labels and title plt.xlabel('Time (s)') plt.ylabel('Sensor Reading') plt.title(‘Example Time Series Sensor Data') plt.legend() 28 The Water Research Foundation # Show the plot plt.show() 5. Run the Script: The project team explains how to save the file and run it from the terminal or command prompt by typing python hello_ai.py. If users use notebooks, the play button can simply be pressed. 4.3 Resources for Learning Python and AI There are entire books and courses dedicated to Python, so learning it all through the ML Toolkit alone is not feasible. To support ongoing learning, the project team provides users with a curated list of resources: • Python.Org Documentation: The official Python documentation is a comprehensive resource for learning Python. (www.python.org) (https://docs.python.org/3/) • W3Schools: An excellent resource for Python tutorials and examples. (https://www.w3schools.com/python/) • Coursera: Offers a variety of courses on Python and AI, including a Python for Everybody specialization. (www.coursera.org/courses?query=python) • edX: Provides courses from top universities on Python and AI. (https://www.edx.org/learn/python) • Kaggle: A platform for data science competitions that also offers free courses on Python and machine learning. (www.kaggle.com/learn) 4.4 Conclusion While teaching the mechanics of code and the theory behind data driven modeling should be left to other specifically dedicated resources, in this chapter, the project team has outlined the key aspects of Python and its relevance to the ML Toolkit for WRRFs. Python has become a standard tool of practice and by emphasizing its ease of use, extensive libraries, supportive community, and versatility, the project team aims to provide users with a solid foundation to begin their AI journey. Leveraging coding tools like Google Colab and Jupyter Notebooks, the ML Toolkit, and the other learning platforms discussed, users can easily get started recreating examples or starting their own projects. The ML Toolkit specifically is designed to elevate the knowledge of those looking to take the next step in leveraging Python for innovative solutions in WRRFS. Integration of Data Driven Process
